findings.text: No test sends an oversized body through a BaseHTTPMiddleware that calls call_next without reading the body first, so exception propagation through its task group is not exercised.
test_application_router_limit_overrides_outer sets router.max_body_size by hand and only asserts 413, which does not prove an override; drop it or replace it with a real Router-level test.
test_declared_content_length_checked_lazily_when_eager_check_disabled asserts that receive is never reached, the same as the eager test, so it does not show the lazy path differs.

coverage.note: Posts 100 KB to the route, mount and router paths with no limit and expects 200; a standalone Router is covered separately.
A body at the limit returns 200 and one byte over returns 413 for each path. test_inner_limit covers the same at route, mount and router level.
Raising is asserted here and lowering in test_inner_limit_lowers_outer, each for route, mount and router. The middleware tests cover nested limits.
Wraps a plain ASGI app; test_under_and_at_limit_passes covers bodies that pass.

Multipart is rejected at len(body)-1 and accepted at len(body). The chunked body and the understated Content-Length are covered by test_application_limit_chunked_without_content_length and test_understated_content_length_does_not_let_body_through.
A declared length of 11 over a limit of 10 returns 413 and the receive call list is empty.
Only the response start is sent. The text/plain body is asserted in test_over_limit_returns_413, and the stream stop in test_body_stream_stops_after_limit_exceeded.
A KeyboardInterrupt mid-parse leaves the temp file closed. The body-limit path is covered by test_multipart_closes_temp_files_when_body_limit_is_hit.
